summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The deterministic gate failed on input validity: a custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object, but the extraction supplies an empty floorplan and no power map. The scenario is Processor A from Li et al. (28 W, 195 mm2, 4 metal and 11 material layers, heat sink 3.3e3 and package 2.0e3 W/m2K) from a vectorless worst-case thermal integrity paper. Its observable is an LP-derived worst-case node temperature over bounded local/global power sets on a 3D multilayer grid. No numeric temperature, unit or ambient value is extractable, so the paper gives only a node-indexed distribution in Fig. 3. Because no Studio result exists, there is no Studio temperature to compare, and comparison_valid is false. No numerical comparison is made, and no replication, agreement or disagreement is claimed. Even if a run were possible, a custom 2D steady run would have no transient trace and would not match the paper's vectorless worst-case LP observable, 3D grid, or solver stack. Only the qualitative point stands: the paper's method is about how uncertain power bounds drive worst-case temperature, but this cannot be tested here. The gate also lists unresolved evidence locators and adversarial/independent review checks, so the extracted inputs are not verified.
limitations: Studio was skipped; there are no simulation outputs or artifacts to assess, and comparison_valid is false.
Floorplan is empty: no block names, positions or dimensions for Processor A; only total die area (195 mm2) is given, and the cited source design (Li et al. [8]) is not in the packet.
No per-block power; only 28 W total, and no published rule exists to split it, so it was not apportioned.
The paper's power is a set of local/global bounds (bL, bU, BL, BU, matrix M) with unknown numeric values, not a single deterministic power map.
The observable is an LP-maximized worst-case per-node temperature over a power-vector set, which differs from a single-power-map steady temperature in aggregation and regime.

The original model is a 3D multilayer grid (11 material layers, 4 metal layers) with equivalent heat-transfer-coefficient boundaries; layer thicknesses and conductivities are missing, and a 2D steady model has different dimensionality and boundary assumptions.
No numeric temperatures, units or ambient temperature are available; Fig. 3 was not digitized, and any digitization would carry axis-reading uncertainty.
Solver and optimizer stack (CHOLMOD, Gurobi LP, spectral sparsification, AMG, weighted Jacobi) does not correspond to any bundled Studio solver.

Table I is column-merged in the text extraction, so applying the shared 3.3e3 and 2.0e3 W/m2K coefficients to Processor A is a layout inference, and the mapping of Table II test cases (25K to 2.0M nodes) to processors is not stated.
No linked code, data or configuration assets were found, and the gate reports unresolved evidence locator, adversarial and independent review checks, so independent verification is absent.
No transient, controller, interposer or reliability data exist in the paper to compare against.
